name: b09-etcd-odd
title: Why etcd uses an odd number of nodes
spec: Two horizontal rows side by side for comparison. Row 1 labelled 3 etcd nodes: three small circles labelled etcd, one crossed out as failed, two remaining with a green tick, text beside: quorum holds, survives one failure. Row 2 labelled 4 etcd nodes: four small circles labelled etcd, one crossed out as failed, three remaining with a green tick, text beside: survives one failure, the extra node adds cost and coordination work. A bracket under both rows with the heading: the same tolerance for one failure. Orange highlight on the extra fourth node in row 2 with the note: adds no failure tolerance. Small monospace label for etcd. A grey note at the bottom: quorum is the majority of members that must agree before a change is saved.
alt: Three and four etcd nodes compared
cap: Odd etcd count: four nodes tolerate no more failures than three, so the extra node adds cost without adding safety.

name: b09-worker-upgrade
title: Order of a Kubernetes upgrade across control plane and workers
spec: A top-to-bottom flow in two lanes. Top lane labelled control plane nodes: box 1 first control plane node: kubeadm upgrade plan, then kubeadm upgrade apply version. Box 2: other control plane nodes: kubeadm upgrade node. Arrow down to the bottom lane. Bottom lane labelled worker nodes, one at a time, with a repeating loop of six small boxes in order: kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets, imageupdate -w --wait, kubeadm upgrade node, systemctl daemon-reload, systemctl restart kubelet, kubectl uncordon. A loop arrow back from the last box to the first labelled next worker. At the end a box: update the Kubernetes version recorded in BCM, because BCM does not update that record itself. Orange highlight on the imageupdate box with the note: update the image too, or a reboot brings back the old version. Monospace for all the commands.
cap: Kubernetes upgrade: upgrade the control plane first, then drain, update and uncordon each worker one at a time.
